description: We are Astro Coders, building an interactive health monitoring system for astronauts on long-duration space missions.
summary:
SOMA is a web app that helps astronauts monitor and act on their own health during long-duration missions. Access is role-based: each crew member signs in with a profile and PIN and sees only their own private data, while the commander also gets a crew-wide view of alerts. Anyone can open Emergency mode without a PIN. They log eight indicators (heart rate, blood pressure, blood sugar, temperature, sleep, mood, fatigue, exercise) and see their status on an interactive body map, with trends compared to their personal baseline.

Alerts come from a deterministic, versioned rule engine, not from AI. Each one shows the reason, who should act, the rule and the NASA/CSA source behind it. When help is far away, Emergency mode gives step-by-step guidance and a simulated report for the ground team. A voice-enabled AI assistant (NVIDIA NIM) explains the data and cites sources, but never diagnoses.

It matters because distance, isolation and radiation make early self-monitoring essential. All data is simulated and labelled as such, and thresholds are illustrative: SOMA is a decision-support prototype, not a medical device.
details:
What it does

SOMA is a responsive web application, for desktop and tablet screens, that helps astronauts on long-duration missions monitor their own health and decide what to do next. It is a self-monitoring and decision-support tool, not a medical device. Distance from Earth means help can be delayed, so the crew needs to notice trends early and act with confidence.

Each crew member picks a profile and signs in with a 4-digit PIN. They can log eight indicators (heart rate, blood pressure, blood sugar, temperature, sleep, mood, fatigue and exercise) one by one or in a daily check-in. The app shows an interactive body map with the status of four body systems, a history with the astronaut's own personal baseline, daily routine reminders, and a notification centre. Every indicator has a measurement guide: how to measure it, why it matters, the typical range and what to do if it looks abnormal.

How it works

Alerts come from a deterministic, versioned rule engine, never from AI. Every alert shows the indicator and value that triggered it, the rule and its version, who should act (crew or ground), suggested actions and the NASA/CSA source that backs it, so it can be traced and reviewed.

An Emergency mode, reachable from every screen without a PIN, guides the crew step by step through scenarios such as chest pain or a collapse, logs each step with a timestamp and prepares a simulated report for the ground team. A Ground support screen shows how a question or handover to flight surgeons would be sent. A mission environment selector (space station or transit) changes the communication delay and the routine timing. An Environment page shows a simulated cabin-radiation and air view.

An optional AI assistant answers questions about the astronaut's saved data and about health topics, cites its sources and has a voice mode (microphone and read-aloud), also inside Emergency mode. It only has read-only tools scoped to the signed-in profile, and it explains what the rule engine decided instead of deciding itself. If the AI provider is unavailable, everything else keeps working.

Roles and privacy

Without a PIN, the shared screen shows only general crew status. With a PIN, an astronaut sees their own private data. The commander also gets a crew-wide view of alerts. Emergency mode is open to everyone on purpose.

Accessibility and responsive design

SOMA adapts to desktop and tablet screens: on a tablet the side navigation moves to a bottom bar and the content reflows to the narrower width. Because astronauts may be tired or in a hurry, readability is built in. Users can switch between a light and a dark theme, increase the text size (large and extra large), add more spacing between letters, words and lines, turn on high contrast and underlined links, and reduce motion. Status never relies on colour alone: every state also has an icon and a text label.

Benefits and impact

SOMA turns isolated readings into trends against the person's own history, explains why something needs attention and points to a source and a safe next step. We think the same ideas (self-monitoring, explainable alerts and guidance when specialists are far away) could also help remote communities on Earth.

Tools and technologies

  • Frontend: React 19, Vite, TanStack Query, Recharts, JavaScript, tested with Cypress.
  • Backend: Node.js 22, Express 5, TypeScript, Prisma 7, zod validation, JWT sessions, bcrypt-hashed PINs, rate limiting. The API is documented with OpenAPI.
  • Data: PostgreSQL on Supabase.
  • AI: OpenAI-compatible SDK pointed at the free NVIDIA NIM API, backend only, with the browser's speech features for voice.
  • Deployment: Vercel, with GitHub Actions.
  • Method: Spec-Driven Development. We wrote a constitution, spec, plan, API contract, tasks and a verification checklist first (all in the repository's docs/ folder), and used AI coding assistants to implement against them.

What is creative

The body map with clickable systems, alerts that carry their own rule, version and source, a personal baseline instead of a generic range, an emergency flow that works with no login and with an assistant that is still guided by the protocol, voice interaction for busy hands, and a design for a tired astronaut: a check-in in under 30 seconds, units always visible, adjustable text and themes, and clear status colours with icons and text.

What we considered

  • Honesty: all data is fictional or simulated and labelled as such, and demo thresholds are labelled illustrative.
  • No overclaiming: we do not integrate any NASA/CSA dataset or instrument (for example CANS). NASA and CSA pages are used as references for risks, hazards and radiation context.
  • Safety: the AI never diagnoses and never computes risk, and the app must work without it.
  • Privacy: only synthetic data is sent to the hosted model, and keys live only in the backend.
  • Accessibility: text size, spacing, contrast, motion and theme can all be adjusted.
  • Limits: the hosted AI service would not be autonomous on a real mission.

Try it:

https://soma-crew.vercel.app/

(no sign-up needed). Choose a fictional crew profile and enter its demo PIN: Ana Vega (commander) 1111, Leo Soler 2222, Inés Vidal 3333, Noa Ríos 4444. Emergency mode needs no PIN.
